yt_posts.topic: Kaspa crossed $1B the same week Coinbase delisted its perps, and the suits started talking
yt_posts.body_style: news breakdown: the week's three Kaspa beats, then the math against the bear
yt_posts.body:
Coinbase delisted the Kaspa perps on September 3, and Kaspa crossed a $1 billion market cap on the way up.

Three things landed in one week and most people only saw one of them.

First, the price. A 25% day, 32% on the week, and a market cap that crossed a billion dollars for the first time in a long time. This whole bear market the only good news in Kaspa land was the dip letting people buy cheaper. Then the chart woke up.

Second, the delisting. Coinbase pulled nine perpetual futures contracts at 13:00 UTC on September 3: Kaspa was on the list next to Popcat and Brett. Spot trading was untouched. And here is the part that matters: the price ran INTO the delisting, not away from it. Whatever was leaning on that perps market was not the thing holding Kaspa up. No premine means no war chest to buy a listing; the exclusion is the receipt of the fair launch, and a derivatives desk dropping the exposure changes nothing about that.

Third, the attention. Two Bitwise executives, including the CIO, plus BitGo, Gemini and Ivan on Tech all publicly engaged Kaspa in the same week. Not a listing, not a product, and I am not going to invent one. But for two years the objection was "nobody knows what it is," and now the people who decide what Wall Street looks at are saying the name out loud. That gives the folks who dropped out a reason to look twice.

Now the math, because there is an influencer out there saying Kaspa never gets past 10 cents again. 28.7 billion max supply, 96.5% of it already mined, no premine, nobody handed a bag at zero. A $3 Kaspa is an $86 billion market cap. In a crypto market heading for tens of trillions, an $86 billion proof of work layer one is not a fantasy, it is a mid-table outcome. Most of my conviction is in Kaspa and none of it gets sold before a parabolic top.

Never financial advice. Never.

So tell me straight in the comments: where does Kaspa top this run, $10 billion, $50 billion, or $100 billion plus? And if you are in the 10-cents camp, say that out loud too, because that is a position and I want to read it.

Hit like and subscribe if you would rather be early than be right in hindsight.

yt_posts.topic: Some things don't die: Nacho, TUT and the comeback tell
yt_posts.body_style: pattern-break essay: the revival receipts, then the filter for which ones come back
yt_posts.body:
They told you the 2024 memes were dead. Nacho the Kat just woke up.

The receipts showed up this week, so here they are, plus the one filter I use to tell a revival from a dead cat bounce.

Start with Nacho. KRC20, Kaspa's own meme, and for the whole bear market there was zero excitement in Kaspa land. Nacho got written off as a relic. Then Kaspa crossed a $1 billion market cap this week and Nacho started moving again, hard. I am not going to put a number on it because the number changes by the hour; go look at the chart.

Then TUT, on BNB Chain. Everybody called that one a dead 2025 meme. In August it ran more than 1,100% to a NEW all-time high. Not a bounce. A new high, after the whole timeline had already buried it.

And the biggest receipt of all: Bitcoin has been declared dead 478 times since 2010. 24 of those obituaries were written this year. Bitcoin is sitting near $80,000. Every single cycle somebody writes the funeral, and every single cycle the funeral is the entry.

Now the honest half, because not everything comes back and I am not going to pretend otherwise. Brett was the first meme on Base to cross a billion dollars. Today it is around $55 million, and it was on the same Coinbase perps delisting list as Kaspa. Some of these are done.

So here is the filter. It is not the chart. It is not the market cap. It is whether the project stayed ACTIVE through the bear market, when there was nothing in it for them. Still posting. Still shipping. The KRC20 communities that kept building are the ones waking up first right now, and that is not a coincidence. A project with dead socials in a bear market is the rug you can see coming; a project that kept the lights on is the one that gets found when new retail walks in and starts looking around.

Some things don't die. Some things get revived. The trick is that the revived ones were never actually dead, they were just ignored.

Never financial advice.

So tell me in the comments: which 2024 or 2025 meme are you betting comes back hardest, a KRC20 like Nacho, TUT, or none of them? And name the one you think is done for good, because that list is just as useful.

Like and subscribe if you want the next comeback before it is on everybody's timeline.
